_comment: What each model costs, keyed by the model id the providers actually send.
Every id in lib/providers/registry.dart should appear here, either with a
price or with "unknown": true. Nothing is ever guessed: a model with no
published per-request price is marked unknown and left out of the total,
which is reported to the user rather than hidden.
unit: tokens  -> in/out are dollars per 1M tokens
image   -> amount is dollars per generated image
second  -> amount is dollars per second of video, minUnits is the
shortest clip the provider will bill for
video   -> amount is a flat fee per generated clip, whatever its length
kchars  -> amount is dollars per 1000 characters of speech
minute  -> amount is dollars per minute of audio
Optional refinements, used when the app knows enough to apply them and
ignored when it does not -- amount is always the fallback:
tiers           -> [{maxMegapixels, amount}, ...] for image models whose
price steps with the frame size. The last entry needs
no ceiling; it is what everything above the previous
one costs.
byResolution    -> {"720p": amount, ...} per second, for video models
whose rate depends on the resolution requested.
audioMultiplier -> what a generated soundtrack multiplies the clip by.
perMillionTokens-> the provider's own published rate, used to price a
finished generation from the token count it reported
rather than from an estimate.
extraInputImage -> charged per reference image past the first.
approx: the published price depends on resolution, quality or plan, and the
number here is one representative point. Shown with a ~ in the UI.
Every video price below is quoted at the resolution the tasks
actually request -- 720p -- because that is what will be billed.
unknown: no public per-request price, or not checked yet. Excluded from the
total and reported as such -- never guessed.
Full working, with the source URL behind every number:
docs/audit-fournisseurs-api.md

_comment_gemini_image: Google prices these per image, by the resolution asked for -- which is
the `image_size` field on the request, so the app knows it before it
sends. `bySize` is that table, exact. Underneath it is token billing at
the rate in `perMillionTokens`, and the published per-image figures are
that rate times the token count of each frame; the two agree to the
cent, which is why these are listed rather than approximated.
`amount` is the 1K figure, for a caller with no size to hand.
Batch pricing is half of all of this and the app never uses it.

_comment_gpt_image: OpenAI publishes a price per image for three frames at three quality
steps, and those nine numbers are in `byFrame` below, keyed
"quality/size". They are exact and are used verbatim whenever the Size
and Quality menus name one of them.
The four larger frames -- 2K and 4K -- have no published per-image
price. Underneath, images are billed as output tokens at 30.00 per
million, and token count goes with area, so those are priced by scaling
the 1024x1024 figure for the same quality by the pixel ratio. A 2048
square is four times the pixels of a 1024 square and comes out four
times the price. That is a model, not a quote, so anything reached that
way is marked approximate in the interface.
`amount` is medium at 1024x1024, which is what a caller with no menu
behind it gets. Quality "auto" lets the model choose the effort; it is

_comment_seedance: Seedance is billed per output token, not per second, and the resolution
is what moves the bill: the same five seconds costs four times as much
at 1080p as at 480p. So each model carries `perMillionTokens` -- its
published rate, which is what BytePlus actually charges -- and the
per-second figures in `byResolution` are that rate evaluated through
BytePlus's own formula for the frames the app asks for:
tokens = width x height x fps / 1024, per second of output
at 24fps and the nominal 16:9 frame of each step: 854x480, 1280x720,
second. That reproduces the worked examples on the pricing page to the
cent, which is why these are listed rather than marked unknown.
`amount` stays the 720p figure so a menu with no shot settings behind it
still quotes something true. List prices throughout, not the promotions
running to 7 and 17 September 2026 -- a discount that lapses is worse to
have baked in than absent. A request carrying a reference *video* is
billed at a lower rate but against a token floor, which cannot be
worked out before sending; hence approx.

_comment_gemini_tts: Google bills TTS by output audio token -- 10.00 per 1M on Flash, 20.00
on Pro -- and the app bills voice-over by the character, so these two
numbers are converted rather than published. Gemini's audio is 25 tokens
a second, and this app reads a script at 2.6 words a second of about six
characters each, so 1000 characters is 64 seconds is 1600 tokens:
0.016 on Flash, 0.032 on Pro. The input text is billed too, at 0.50 and
1.00 per 1M tokens, which is under a tenth of a cent for a whole ad and
is left out. Marked approx because the speaking rate is ours, not
Google's -- a fast read costs less than this says and a slow one more.
